sources.text: O Xbox Game Pass é um dos serviços de assinatura de games mais democráticos da atualidade, já que é possível acessá-lo de diferentes plataformas — incluindo os próprios, consoles da Microsoft, assim como no PC, nuvem, celulares, tablets e até Smart TVs Samsung e LG com modelos de 2022 para cá. Felizmente, seu catálogo também é atualizado quase que semanalmente, trazendo inúmeras opções para os assinantes aproveitarem — e o melhor de tudo: gastando pouco em comparação às novas tendências de preços da indústria. Se veio em busca de novos jogos para jogar através do Xbox Game Pass , está no lugar certo. O serviço ganhou um reforço de peso esta semana com a chegada de cinco títulos para os assinantes aproveitarem. Confira abaixo mais informações sobre as novas aventuras! Disponível no lançamento no Xbox Game Pass, Warhammer Survivors é um jogo de ação no estilo bullet heaven, inspirado em Vampire Survivors . Com visual em pixel art, o game coloca os jogadores contra grandes hordas de inimigos, utilizando armas, habilidades e personagens inspirados no universo de Warhammer . Também disponível no lançamento no Xbox Game Pass, Tanuki: Pon’s Summer coloca os jogadores no controle de Pon, um guaxinim que precisa restaurar um santuário antes do Festival Tanuki. Para cumprir a missão, será necessário entregar encomendas de bicicleta, fazer amizades e ajudar os moradores em atividades como preparar sushi e participar de lutas de sumô. Outro game a compor o Game Pass no lançamento, Hope in the City é uma aventura de mistério protagonizada por Hope Song, uma jovem de 17 anos que descobre o desaparecimento dos pais ao voltar para casa. Durante a investigação, os jogadores precisam transformar desenhos em pistas e desvendar segredos cada vez mais misteriosos sobre a família da protagonista. Thronefall é um jogo de estratégia minimalista em que os jogadores precisam construir e administrar um reino durante o dia e protegê-lo de invasores durante a noite. Para sobreviver às ondas de inimigos, será necessário equilibrar a economia, fortalecer as defesas, recrutar soldados e participar diretamente dos combates. Por fim, em John Carpenter’s Toxic Commando , até quatro jogadores podem se unir em uma aventura cooperativa de ação e sobrevivência contra hordas de zumbis. Ambientado em um mundo tomado por criaturas, o game apresenta missões em cenários semiabertos e coloca os jogadores em uma jornada para tentar salvar a humanidade. stories.title: PS5 QSSR Updates Revealed for Marvel's Spider-Man 2, Arc Raiders, and More
stories.summary: Sony has confirmed Marvel's Spider-Man 2, Arc Raiders, and four more games are receiving QSSR support on base PS5s.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: PS5 QSSR Updates Revealed for Marvel's Spider-Man 2, Arc Raiders, and More
sources.text: Sony has confirmed Marvel's Spider-Man 2 , Arc Raiders , and four more games are receiving QSSR support on base PS5s. The list of six newcomers joining the small-but-growing group of supported games was unveiled in a PlayStation.Blog post . In addition to confirmation that incoming updates will add QSSR (Quick Spectral Super Resolution), the post included testimonials from each of the studios' developers, who shared how the tech will impact visuals. When Sony pulled back the curtain on QSSR in October, it came with confirmation that it had already been implemented in Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yōtei. Now, we know that Insomniac's Marvel's Spider-Man 2, Remedy Entertainment's Control Resonant , Embark Studios' Arc Raiders and The Finals , Hello Games' No Man's Sky , and Expression Games' Hell Let Loose: Vietnam will soon take advantage of the AI upscaling tech. In the case of Marvel's Spider-Man 2, QSSR is available as part of a new update that's out now. "Having seen great results integrating QSSR in Marvel’s Wolverine, our team decided to bring it to Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 as well, in an update that’s live now!" Insomniac head of technology Mike Fitzgerald said. "We’re excited for players to swing back into our 2023 title and see QSSR’s exciting image stability and sharpness benefits in both Fidelity and Performance modes." Remedy said QSSR will bring noticeable improvements in image stability and fine detail when it launches in a new update in December. Hello Games founder Sean Murray, meanwhile, promised that players can look forward to No Man's Sky looking "sharper, cleaner, and more beautiful" at the "best possible framerate" in the next few weeks. When exactly The Finals, Arc Raiders, and Hell Let Loose: Vietnam will receive their updates has yet to be announced. "With the new QSSR coming soon to ARC Raiders and The Finals, we can deliver increased sharpness, better environmental clarity, and overall visual improvements to even more PlayStation players," Embark said. "We are very happy to see Sony’s continued investment in PlayStation technology translate into meaningful improvements for all players, bringing more immersive experiences across the PlayStation ecosystem." Sony then teased that developers interested in using QSSR are "just getting started." More PS5 games are set to receive similar updates in the coming months, though which titles will join the list remains to be seen. Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

After a distress signal from a derelict ship is picked up, you and your crew quickly get embroiled into the story of an abandoned settlement, a […]

sources.name: PlayStation Blog
sources.title: The Outer Worlds 2’s first DLC arrives December 2
sources.text: The first in a two-part Side Effects Guaranteed narrative adventure arrives soon, with part two coming spring 2027. The time has come to expand on the experience for The Outer Worlds 2 with the first of a two-part story expansion, Side Effects Guaranteed, arriving on December 2. After a distress signal from a derelict ship is picked up, you and your crew quickly get embroiled into the story of an abandoned settlement, a power struggle for the future of the Sub Rosa criminal organization, and the fate of a team who has been subjected to something that will cause them all to die from explosive cell death. Really, it’s more a liquefaction than explosion, but it means death nonetheless. A brand new story filled with moral quandaries and consequences big and small isn’t the only thing you’ll experience in the first DLC. An Earth Directorate Commander should always be sure to have a weapon at their side, and there are five new weapons to add to the arsenal. Such as the Immobilizer. Think of it like a gun that makes gravity forget to exist around its target, allowing them to float in the air, so you can switch to another weapon and pick them off as you like. Great for combining with grenades for anti-gravity explosions or the Tactical Time Dilation device for slowing down time and getting some critical shots in. There is also the 1/6 Resolver that allows every sixth bullet that is fired from it to pack an extra special punch. For those who built their characters just right, they won’t have to empty the gun every time to get that critical hit, either. Other weapons include a weapon that does additional damage to creatures, a special Tossball Stick, and a new plasma weapon for some energy fun. Yet it isn’t all about the weapons. Side Effects Guaranteed will also bring with it a level cap increase up to 36, new perks, new flaws, and a new Sub Rosa radio station with 20 new songs. There is also the all-new region of Elysium Valley to explore with unique quests and new facilities to make your way through. That’s a lot of new! While the events of the DLC do trigger right before the point of no return in the main game, there is also a way to jump easily into the action. From the main menu if you start a new game, you will see an option to start Side Effects Guaranteed directly. This will load a pre-made character at level 27 that you can assign skill points and perks to so you can experience the DLC however you’d like and get started right away. Not happy with the character you made (or the one you already have)? Coming to everyone at the same time as the release of Side Effects Guaranteed is a new update that will allow players to respec their character at any time. And for those who want more skills to play around with, a new addition to the custom game options allows you to adjust how many skill points you get per level. Find the balance that is right for you. Or become an Earth Director demi-god. Your worlds, your way. But remember, however you decide to deal with Sub Rosa or the subjects of Elysium Valley will have consequences. Side effects, some might say, that will lead directly into the next installment of The Outer Worlds 2 two-part story expansion when it releases in the spring of 2027. Until then, may skill catch you where fortune fails. Side Effects Guaranteed releases on December 2nd or is available in the Premium Edition or Premium Edition Upgrade for The Outer Worlds 2 .

sources.name: Xbox Wire BR
sources.title: Efeitos colaterais estão garantidos no primeiro DLC de The Outer Worlds 2, que chega em 2 de dezembro
sources.text: Um sinal de socorro leva você e sua tripulação da Incognito até uma nave abandonada, onde vocês encontram os tripulantes em animação suspensa. Tudo indica que há algo de errado, especialmente a poça do que muito provavelmente já foi uma pessoa. Você recupera uma mensagem em vídeo deixada pela capitã da nave, que explica que a tripulação foi contaminada por algo durante um roubo e que, se não encontrarem uma cura, isso causará uma morte celular explosiva. E, por morte celular explosiva, ela quer dizer algo mais parecido com uma… “liquefação”. Pelo jeito da poça no chão: é liquefação mesmo. Esse é o cenário para o lançamento da primeira parte de uma expansão narrativa em DLC de The Outer Worlds 2 , dividida em duas partes, em 2 de dezembro. Em Side Effects Guaranteed, a mensagem em vídeo que você encontrou leva até Gordon Hazen, um dos principais agentes da Sub Rosa, uma organização criminosa formada por pessoas que compartilham dos mesmos ideais e escolheram viver roubando das diversas facções em vez de trabalhar para elas. Gordon, por sua vez, envia você para Elysium Valley, uma nova região de Eden que abriga um assentamento de antigos súditos do Protetorado, esquecidos por seus líderes. Ele acredita que eles podem ter as respostas para salvar sua tripulação. Embora prefira a diplomacia à violência, ele precisa que você faça o que for necessário para conseguir as informações de que precisa. Mas Gordon não é o único interessado em Elysium Valley. Outro agente da Sub Rosa, Algernon Lankester, quer recrutar você para ajudá-lo a explorar os súditos em benefício próprio. O destino dos súditos, dos agentes congelados da Sub Rosa e o futuro da própria organização estão nas suas mãos, nosso intrépido Comandante. No entanto, uma nova história não será a única novidade de Side Effects Guaranteed quando o DLC for lançado daqui a algumas semanas. Além de explorar a nova região de Elysium Valley, os jogadores vão encontrar novas ameaças, como canídeos ferozes e sprats primitivos. O que é um sprat primitivo? É só um sprat normal, mas cerca de 100 vezes maior. Com certeza, eles são tão amigáveis quanto seus primos bem menores e vão perdoar todas as vezes em que você atirou neles “sem querer” enquanto explorava Arcadia. Com essas novas ameaças, vem a possibilidade de deixar seu Comandante ainda mais forte e, é claro, com mais defeitos (mas no bom sentido). O limite de nível aumentará de 30 para 36, trazendo mais pontos de habilidade para diversificar sua configuração de personagem. Poder chegar ao nível 36 também significa que você poderá adquirir mais três vantagens, com 15 vantagens inéditas adicionadas às opções disponíveis. Também serão introduzidos quatro novos defeitos que podem mudar a forma de jogar com seu Comandante, como “Lethally Tolerant”, que reconhece sua resistência acumulada a substâncias químicas e aumenta sua toxicidade máxima. Isso é ótimo na hora, mas, se você sofrer um colapso de toxicidade, morrerá instantaneamente. Outro exemplo é “Must Have Been the Wind”, que marca um “alvo de assassinato” em um grupo de combate. Eliminar o alvo concede um bônus de 20% no dano e na velocidade até o fim do combate, mas não conseguir eliminá-lo ou atacar alguém que não seja o alvo aplica ao jogador uma penalidade de 10% no dano e na velocidade por 30 segundos. São recompensas que realmente vêm acompanhadas de grandes riscos. Side Effects Guaranteed também trará novas armas, novas armaduras e novos trajes para cada um dos companheiros, além de uma estação de rádio inédita comandada pela Sub Rosa, com 20 novas músicas para o jogo. Para quem quiser ir direto à ação no DLC, será adicionado um novo ponto de partida alternativo ao menu principal ao selecionar um novo jogo, permitindo começar com um arquivo de jogo salvo personalizado que coloca você no início do DLC. Inicie o jogo, distribua seus pontos de habilidade e de vantagem e aproveite Side Effects Guaranteed sem demora! Essa aventura repleta de conteúdo, com uma história profunda e sistemas para criar seu Comandante ideal, preparará o terreno para o próximo DLC de The Outer Worlds 2 , que chegará no segundo trimestre de 2027. As escolhas que você fizer terão impacto direto no próximo DLC. A primeira parte dessa história que se desenrola ao longo da expansão, Side Effects Guaranteed, será lançada em 2 de dezembro e também está incluída na Edição Premium ou no Upgrade para a Edição Premium de The Outer Worlds 2 .

stories.title: Crimson Desert studio Pearl Abyss now implementing AI "throughout our entire development pipeline"
stories.summary: Gen-AI assets were removed from Crimson Desert in March

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: Crimson Desert studio Pearl Abyss now implementing AI "throughout our entire development pipeline"
sources.text: Gen-AI assets were removed from Crimson Desert in March It's a sad reality that several major games companies have either tried to use AI in development, or are actively doing so. Pearl Abyss, the studio behind this year's Crimson Desert , can now be counted among them, confirming the technology is being integrated across the business. The publisher and developer revealed this in a recent Earnings Letter . "We are integrating AI technologies to enhance development productivity and overall quality," Pearl Abyss writes. "AI is being utilized across various stages of development – including the automation of repetitive tasks, content creation support, and test optimization – and we are expanding its implementation throughout our entire development pipeline." It's worth remembering, Crimson Desert players dragged the game for having apparent generative-AI assets back in March. A subsequent update removed them, and Pearl Abyss issued an apology for allowing the game to ship with those elements still intact. Apparently that episode hasn't deterred leadership from incorporating the technology into even more facets of the design process. "We view AI not as a substitute for human developers, but as a tool to elevate development efficiency and quality," Pearl Abyss adds. "We will continue to expand our application of AI to deliver higher-fidelity games to the market more expeditiously." That much is good to hear, but my cynicism remains. The simple fact is AI is a poor substitute for creative iteration, and while it may speed up certain parts of game production, it's far too easy for audio, visual or mechanical elements to be among the corners that wound up cut as a result of the technology. For the time-being, fanbases are fervently against generative assets in their games. Whether they be Call of Duty , Battlefield 6 or Crimson Desert, once AI is noticed, you can't put the genie back in the bottle. Pearl Abyss confirms that the upcoming Pokemon-like creature-collecting game DokeV is being made using AI to an extent. "AI serves strictly as a tool to support concept validation and pipeline productivity, while the core gameplay experience and actual content creation remain fully driven by our development team," the letter says. Not the most auspicious update, but we'll see what emerges when the project is on show. Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more Crimson Desert is among the "most technically ambitious games we’ve seen" in 10 years but is overshadowed by "the same safe, conventional AAA games," says Palworld lead. Anthony is an Irish entertainment and games journalist, now based in Glasgow. He previously served as Senior Anime Writer at Dexerto and News Editor at The Digital Fix, on top of providing work for Variety, IGN, Den of Geek, PC Gamer, and many more. Besides Studio Ghibli, horror movies, and The Muppets, he enjoys action-RPGs, heavy metal, and pro-wrestling. He interviewed Animal once, not that he won’t stop going on about it or anything. sources.title: Crimson Desert studio is implementing AI "throughout our entire development pipeline," and expects DokeV to launch in 2028
sources.text: "This enables a more efficient allocation of development resources and enhances overall production speed." Crimson Desert and DokeV developer Pearl Abyss is planning to further integrate generative AI into its workflow. The South Korean studio said as much in its latest quarterly Earnings Letter , explaining that it had previously "validated game systems only after implementing them manually." Now, Pearl Abyss is using AI "to rapidly validate diverse design concepts prior to actual implementation," and argues the move "enables a more efficient allocation of development resources and enhances overall production speed." "However, AI serves strictly as a tool to support concept validation and pipeline productivity, while the core gameplay experience and actual content creation remain fully driven by our development team," the developer said. When Crimson Desert first launched, players spotted a crop of suspicious in-game images that looked like they were prompted into existence . Pearl Abyss soon explained that some "2D visual props" were generated with AI tools , but were always intended to be replaced with human-made art, before quickly patching them out of the hit open-world game. It seems Pearl Abyss is now even more keen on the controversial tech, however: "We are integrating AI technologies to enhance development productivity and overall quality. AI is being utilized across various stages of development - including the automation of repetitive tasks, content creation support, and test optimization - and we are expanding its implementation throughout our entire development pipeline. We view AI not as a substitute for human developers, but as a tool to elevate development efficiency and quality. We will continue to expand our application of AI to deliver higher-fidelity games to the market more expeditiously." Elsewhere in the letter, the studio said its previously announced creature-collector DokeV is "targeting a launch in the second half of 2028" and we should hear more about it within the year. DokeV was initially targeting a 2023 launch a few years ago. Meanwhile, Crimson Desert is being prepped for a Nintendo Switch 2 launch "in the first half of next year." The use of generative AI in game development has been a hot topic for years, though it's only become more prevalent in recent months as 'AI slop' floods Steam and big companies like Epic Games proudly adopt the tech . A recent report even estimated that around 40 percent of active developers use AI tools in their work.

sources.title: Don't like AI in games? Crimson Desert studio Pearl Abyss ain't care: it's expanding AI use 'throughout our entire development pipeline'
sources.text: Pearl Abyss apologized for the presence of AI-generated art in Crimson Desert earlier this year, but it's not slowing down. Earlier this year, Pearl Abyss apologized for the presence of AI-generated art in Crimson Desert—not because it had used generative AI, mind, but because players saw it. And it seems like the odds we might see more of it in the future are going up, as the studio said in its Q3 2026 earnings letter (via Eurogamer ) that it will be going even deeper on AI-powered development in the future. The first reference to AI comes midway through the letter: "While we previously validated game systems only after implementing them manually, we now utilize AI to rapidly validate diverse design concepts prior to actual implementation," it states. "This enables a more efficient allocation of development resources and enhances overall production speed." The studio immediately clarified, though, that AI "serves strictly as a tool to support concept validation and pipeline productivity," and that gameplay and content development "remain fully driven by our development team." The future will see more of the same, with the same caveats. "We are integrating AI technologies to enhance development productivity and overall quality," Pearl Abyss writes. "AI is being utilized across various stages of development—including the automation of repetitive tasks, content creation support, and test optimization—and we are expanding its implementation throughout our entire development pipeline. "We view AI not as a substitute for human developers, but as a tool to elevate development efficiency and quality. We will continue to expand our application of AI to deliver higher-fidelity games to the market more expeditiously." That essentially repeats what Pearl Abyss said in February when players discovered the presence of generative AI art in Crimson Desert : It acknowledged that "some 2D visual props" had been created by AI during the early stages of development, but said they were supposed to be replaced "following final work and review by our art and development teams, with work that aligned with our quality standards and creative direction." The studio also admitted that it had not "clearly disclosed our use of AI" in the development process, and promised to be more transparent about it in the future. This letter certainly could be seen as a step in that direction. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. Pearl Abyss also said it aims to release DokeV, the " weird GTA: Babies game " revealed in 2021, sometime in the second half of 2028. stories.title: Quote of the Day by GTA 6 CEO: "Grand Theft Auto franchise is probably the most valuable IP"

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: Quote of the Day by GTA 6 CEO: "Grand Theft Auto franchise is probably the most valuable IP"
sources.text: The CEO of the publishers behind GTA 6, Take-Two Interactive, isn't quite ready to go on his victory lap just yet, but he is once again enjoying what he thinks might be the most valuable entertainment IP in the world. Speaking to David Rubenstein, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick was asked about the size of of GTA 6's impending launch. In traditional fashion, Zelnick remained pretty humble, telling Rubenstein that "we never claim success before it occurs." In this instance, he notes, Take-Two and Rockstar have had plenty of success together. "It's true that GTA 5 was a massive hit," he admits. "It sold in over 230 million units, and we believe the Grand Theft Auto franchise as a whole is probably the most valuable intellectual property in the entertainment business, of any type, because of its enormous reach to consumers worldwide." Zelnick's argument is a potent one, but it's also a little hard to pin down. Off the top of my head, Pokémon and Marvel have certainly generated more money, but that's admittedly off the back of many hundreds more releases (and many more decades, in Marvel's case). Clearly, however, neither of those franchises can match the billions of dollars off a single launch that GTA 6 is set to make next week, or the other billions that the long tail of GTA Online is likely to secure. Pound-for-pound, GTA certainly sends those other heavyweights back to the corner, even if the 13-year gap between releases might be hurting a little. Despite his quiet confidence in the brand, however, Zelnick is still refusing to count his chickens before they hatch. "The team at Rockstar has been working diligently to try to create something extraordinary with Grand Theft Auto 6," he says. "I believe they will, I'm very optimistic, but as for success, we'll have to wait until November 19 and beyond." sources.title: Ubisoft is reportedly making a new Rainbow Six Vegas game, nearly two decades after Vegas 2
sources.text: Ubisoft is reportedly working on a new Rainbow Six Vegas game 18 years after the last entry in the series. According to Insider Gaming , the project is in early development at Ubisoft Montreal under the codename Spades. It’s one of three new projects reportedly in production at the studio, and sources suggest a second of those is also set in the Rainbow Six universe. Eurogamer hasn’t been able to verify the report. It’s not yet clear what form the new game will take, but Insider Gaming’s sources said it's "likely Vegas 3 rather than a remake" of an existing game. Insider Gaming expects it will be several years before Ubisoft officially announces a new Vegas game. Rainbow Six Vegas launched in 2006, followed by Rainbow Six Vegas 2 in 2008. Since then, the series has centred on 2015's Rainbow Six Siege, and in August, Ubisoft announced Rainbow Six Tactics, a single-player, turn-based spin-off from Ubisoft Paris due in 2027. Rainbow Six now sits under Vantage Studios, the Ubisoft subsidiary set up last year that also oversees Assassin’s Creed and Far Cry , and in which Tencent holds a 26.32 percent stake. Last week, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on two new Assassin's Creed games : one set in ancient Rome, and a mobile spin-off set in Jerusalem. The leak came less than a week after Ubisoft issued a statement about the future of the Assassin's Creed series , insisting there are currently no new remakes of the series' past games in the works.

stories.title: New Grand Theft Auto 6 trailer is for a TV show that exists within Grand Theft Auto 6
stories.summary: Macca and Friends is coming to Weazel TV on November 19.

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: New Grand Theft Auto 6 trailer is for a TV show that exists within Grand Theft Auto 6
sources.text: Macca and Friends is coming to Weazel TV on November 19. Get ready for some wheels within wheels, as DiscussingFilm has revealed an animated trailer for a Grand Theft Auto 6 TV show—and I don't mean a trailer for a show about GTA 6, but a trailer for a show in GTA 6. Macca and Friends, as the show is known, follows the adventures of a gang of anthropomorphic Floridian—Leonidan, I suppose—animals as they try to find their way in the world, accompanied to some extent by a beefed-up cop. The animals are cops too. It's a bit like Scooby Doo, maybe, but more egalitarian. Rockstar hasn't said anything about the show, but this isn't the first appearance of Macca: A Macca and Friends mural appeared in a real-life BurgerShot that was set up in Miami's Kaseya Center in October, and a billboard for the show was erected in Miami as well. Both advertised Macca and Friends as "coming November 19 on Weazel," a Fox-like television channel that exists within the GTA universe. How much of an actual, full-on show Rockstar has constructed here, I cannot say. Remedy has done similar things with its games, but those are just brief snippets delivering a little bit of meta narrative ; Rockstar, by comparison, gave us multiple stand-up comedy shows in GTA 5 and black-and-white films in Red Dead Redemption 2… not to mention, fully animated horse testicles . In that light, is it hard to believe they may have created an entire animated series for GTA 6? It might just be another blast from the GTA marketing machine—Rockstar is also literally renting the Miami Heat to promote its game, after all. At this point I don't think anything's off the table. PlayStation and Xbox owners will find out in less than a week: Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19. A PC release date (or any kind of PC announcement at all) remains elusive. stories.title: The Game Awards 2026 Will Stream Live on Roblox for the First Time, Complete With Voting and Virtual Merch
stories.summary: The Game Awards is coming to Roblox for the first time this December, complete with live voting, virtual merchandise, and the opportunity to experience the whole thing alongside other players.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: The Game Awards 2026 Will Stream Live on Roblox for the First Time, Complete With Voting and Virtual Merch
sources.text: The Game Awards is coming to Roblox for the first time this December, giving fans another way to watch Geoff Keighley's annual gaming shindig, complete with live voting, virtual merchandise, and the opportunity to experience the whole thing alongside other players. The Game Awards 2026 will stream live on Roblox starting Thursday, December 10, marking the first time an external awards show has been livestreamed on the platform. The broadcast will take place in The Block, Roblox's virtual event venue, while the actual ceremony takes place at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. There's a catch, though. Only Roblox users aged 18 and older will be able to attend the virtual watch party. Those who are old and wizened enough to take part will be able to watch the entire broadcast, including the usual assortment of world premieres, new game announcements, awards, and musical performances. Fans will also be able to vote, interact with other viewers, and claim virtual merchandise, although exactly what that merchandise will look like remains to be seen. Official category voting will also be available ahead of the ceremony, with further details about the Roblox experience expected closer to the event. On December 10th, #TheGameAwards makes history as the show will stream live in @Roblox for the first time. Fans 18+ will be able to watch, vote and interact LIVE alongside gaming's biggest night. More details coming soon. https://t.co/ouVtxXt7yV The Block is no stranger to hosting major events. The virtual venue has previously been home to the Roblox Innovation Awards, alongside music experiences featuring artists including Billie Eilish, The Rolling Stones, and (K-pop fan hyperventilating) Stray Kids . The Game Awards 2026 takes place December 10, with Geoff Keighley once again at the helm. There's no word yet on exactly how the virtual merchandise or interactive elements will work, but more details are promised in the coming weeks. It will also be available to stream through Disney+ . At the very least, watching The Game Awards in Roblox should make for an interesting alternative to sitting through several hours of announcements while arguing about Game of the Year in a group chat. Now you can do it surrounded by avatars instead. Rachel Weber is the Head of Editorial Development at IGN and an elder millennial. She's been a professional nerd since 2006 when she got her start on Official PlayStation Magazine in the UK, and has since worked for GamesIndustry.Biz, Rolling Stone and GamesRadar. She loves horror, horror movies, horror games, Red Dead Redemption 2, and her Love and Deepspace boyfriends.

stories.title: Nintendo Just Accidentally Got Every Zelda Nerd’s Hopes Up

sources.name: Kotaku
sources.title: Nintendo Just Accidentally Got Every Zelda Nerd’s Hopes Up
sources.text: Nintendo Switch Online The Legend of Zelda For the last two weeks, an official Nintendo website has erroneously suggested that The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds is available on Nintendo Switch Online. [ALBW] Found this on Nintendo's website today, probably doesn't mean anything though. by u/vertexjrpg in zelda This was shared today by Reddit user vertexjrpg , who posted a screenshot of what they saw. Kotaku was able to confirm that the NSO indicator was there as recently as this morning, and per Wayback Machine was there as far back as November 4, which is when the “History” section of the 40th anniversary website was first added. As of this afternoon, it has been removed . Kotaku has reached out to Nintendo for comment. Does this mean anything? Probably not. Most likely, this is a case of whoever made this website putting a button that should have gone somewhere else in the wrong place. It happens. But there’s always the minute possibility that this is somehow a sign of something to come. With GameCube and GBA games now viable fodder for NSO inclusion as of the Switch 2, next on the list would be Wii, Wii U, DS, and 3DS. Right now, the only way to (legally, officially) play games on any of these consoles is by owning the physical system, and either a physical copy of a given game or a digital one downloaded from back when their respective online shops were still active. So it’s not exactly easy for a Zelda fan, especially someone coming in more recently with Ocarina of Time , to experience excellent games like A Link Between Worlds . I’m not optimistic we’ll see 3DS games on NSO any time soon, but I want to believe it is an eventual inevitability, if only so I can go back at will to an awful lot of otherwise inaccessible PokÃ©mon games. As long as I don’t have to sign up for a third, more expensive subscription tier to make it happen. Donât miss the latest reviews, news and tips. Sign up for our free newsletter. I'm not saying I *would* chew them, I'm just saying... We'll create...a constellation...of our very own...

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: Nintendo just broke the Zelda timeline by 10,000 years
sources.text: As the refounding theory finally starts to settle in, now we've got a shifting Great Calamity to deal with The Legend of Zelda timeline has gotten yet another confusing new update, shifting the events leading to Breath of the Wild by 9,900 years and directly contradicting established lore. It's such an about-face for the existing story that series fans are pretty sure it's just a mistake, but the new word comes straight from Nintendo of America, which is often treated as gospel. The Zelda timeline splits into three different branches based on the end of Ocarina of Time, but those branches all converge in the misty history leading up to the events of Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom. Earlier this year, Nintendo updated the Japanese version of the timeline and made clear that the founding of Hyrule depicted in flashback during Tears of the Kingdom shows the start of a new Hyrule , well after the one depicted in Ocarina of Time and other games has faded into history. Now, Nintendo of America has updated the official English-language timeline to confirm the refounding – well, I say "confirm" but I'm sure it'll remain contentiously debated among the most dedicated purists. Either way, the update has made another curious tweak to the rest of the backstory. Up until now, we've understood the timeline depicted in Tears of the Kingdom's flashbacks like this: Hyrule is (re)founded, Ganondorf appears to invade, and is sealed away as part of the Imprisoning War. Untold generations pass, and the evil entity known as Calamity Ganon eventually emerges and ravages the kingdom before being pushed back by Sheikah technology. 10,000 years pass from that Great Calamity, and that brings us to Breath of the Wild. Calamity Ganon reemerges, Link hibernates for 100 years, and the game begins. According to the new timeline, the Imprisoning War happens, 9,900 years pass, and then the Great Calamity happens. Then it's just 100 years before Ganon reemerges – now referred to as "the second Great Calamity" – kicking off Link's century-long hibernation leading into Breath of the Wild. In other words, the first Great Calamity, which was originally placed 10,000 years before Breath of the Wild, now takes place just a century or two before the game's events. This is despite the fact that Breath of the Wild is full of people trying to unlock the secrets of a pre-Calamity world that's long since faded into myth. How are Zelda fans taking the sudden break in established lore? Well, you can read the Reddit threads for yourself, but I imagine you can already guess the tone of the responses. The Zelda timeline is notoriously convoluted, and while Nintendo has kept it up since at least 2003, Shigeru Miyamoto always maintained that it's "not that important to us." Sign up to our Switch 2 Spotlight newsletter to make sure you get the very latest news on Nintendo's new console and its games every week Perhaps that's why Eiji Aonuma shut down attempts to add further nods to the timeline Ocarina of Time , and why a new official timeline update can so suddenly make an astronomical shift to established lore. Don't worry – regardless of how this detail shakes out, I'm sure the timeline will be broken in all-new ways soon enough. Nintendo pulled back the horror from one of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake's most terrifying enemies: "Maybe we've gone a step too far." Dustin Bailey joined the GamesRadar team as a Staff Writer in May 2022, and is currently based in Missouri. He's been covering games (with occasional dalliances in the worlds of anime and pro wrestling) since 2015, first as a freelancer, then as a news writer at PCGamesN for nearly five years. His love for games was sparked somewhere between Metal Gear Solid 2 and Knights of the Old Republic, and these days you can usually find him splitting his entertainment time between retro gaming, the latest big action-adventure title, or a long haul in American Truck Simulator.
